The accepted exact coefficient identity (40.76) therefore applies to these squarefree products, including the unit: AU(g)=μ(g)(2𝟏Ng≤U−1),Ng≤7U.(40.95) For completeness, every proper divisor of a nonunit good g has norm at most Ng/7≤U. integration.detail: 40.25 The coherent signed main and its remaining inputs The physical sixth-power-free comparison in Section 40.27 provides a new positive upper bound. We now collect the exact coherent reductions that it can enter. They preserve the original mean and all raw masks; none proves the target by a scalar cancellation assertion. Use the complete original good squarefree annulus and common complex profile of Section 40.23. Write 𝒰 for the actual nonzero literal rows, wu≥0, Rw=∑uwu and B=∥W∥∞. Retain fixed S,ν, all internal row masks and (40.52). Every identity below is a raw A–A identity; principal residues still require their separate assembly. Classical operator specializations are only for the original unweighted A6=1 rows, or their already justified bounded natural multiplicities. First there is a useful distinction between two auxiliary kernels. Let Kall be KS of (40.57) with the U-smooth restriction on its squarefree f removed, retaining (f,u)=1 and exactly AU(fa) in every Tf. Set P2=∑uwu∑p∉SNp>U∑q∉S,Nq>Uq∤u|W(NpNq/D)|2,KS=Kall+P2,0≤P2/D≤3584B2Rw.(40.89) Here (p,q) is ordered, p=q is allowed, and only q has the stated row mask. This is distinct from the original unordered, distinct-prime C2 in (40.58). In particular S1AA=K0−KallD+Δ+C2−P2D.(40.90) At H≤D3/4 the error in this new auxiliary main is at most 236800B2Rw. The old 233216B2Rw bound for (K0−KS)/D is unchanged. The physical comparison in (40.112) estimates the new combined main, in its stated A6=1 scope, without estimating its two summands separately. The prime-discrepancy clauses below additionally require U≥7. Define ES(t)=πKS(t)−Li⁡2(t),Li⁡2(t)=∫2tdvlog⁡v,M1(W)=max⁡{B,∥xW′(x)∥∞}. The count is of prime ideals outside fixed S, including distinct conjugate ideals and inert prime norms. Put Q(t)=∑fgoodSFfU-smoothμ(f)∑u∈𝒰(f,u)=1wu|Tf(t;u)|2,𝒥=∫U∞Q(t)log⁡tdt. Proposition 40.13 (A joint form retaining its mean). On the finite space of good squarefree g with Ng≤2D/U, let bg(t)=AU(g)ν(g)W(Ngt/D),(𝖱c)(u)=wu∑gcgχg(u),(𝖯fc)g=𝟏f∣gcg. With ordinary counting ℓ2 norms, Q(t)=b(t)*ℳUb(t),ℳU=∑fU-smoothμ(f)𝖯f𝖱*𝖱𝖯f,t≥U.(40.91) The matrix is self-adjoint, with no positivity assertion. The exact prime substitution is KS=𝒥+ℰPIT,ℰPIT=−ES(U)Q(U)−∫U∞ES(t)Q′(t)dt.(40.92) The endpoint excludes Np=U exactly. It must remain. For any true arbitrary-coefficient row norm λ*(L), use the direct unit-column value Rw on 1/2≤L<1. On the active range 1≤L≤D/U, the current original two-pivot bound is the minimum in Proposition 40.19; it is not a theorem for arbitrary row weights. Let λ#(D/T) dominate this norm on the two adjacent active length dyads. Then |ℰPIT|D≪ϵ(HD)ϵM1(W)2{|ES(U)|Uλ*(D/U)+∑T𝔡2(T)λ#(D/T)},(40.93) where T=2jU<2D and 𝔡2(T)2=∫T2T|ES(t)|2t−3dt. This is a sufficient-input budget, not an asserted power estimate for 𝔡2 or for the endpoint. The pointwise version retains λ*(D/U)+∫1/2D/Uλ*(L)dL/L, with the current minimum inside that integral. On good rough-prime columns the exact quadratic-form compression is Π𝒫ℳUΠ𝒫=Π𝒫𝖱*𝖱Π𝒫. This is not an invariant-subspace assertion: off-block couplings remain and can cancel its contribution. Radial Mellin Parseval likewise retains equal-norm ideal correlations, including their derivatives; it neither orthogonalizes orientations nor permits deleting their mean. Even exact prime density leaves K0−𝒥 to estimate. Proposition 40.14 (A sufficient smooth-divisor tail cutoff). For the original unweighted A6=1 two-pivot rows put R=A1A2, Mrow=max⁡(A1,A2). Restrict the smooth f sums in K0,KS to Nf>Y≥1. The inherited positive input gives |K0>Y|D≪ϵ(HD)ϵB2{R+DRMrowY+D2/3RMrow1/3Y2/3},KS>Y=0(Y≥2D/U).(40.94) If R≪H, a sufficient target-size tail cutoff is Y≥max⁡{1,2DU,DRMrowH,DR3/2Mrow1/2H3/2}. This is a coarse inherited sufficient bound, not signed cancellation or an optimal localization. The smooth incidence divisor f is not the original column-pair gcd h. Theorem 40.15 (A conditional input diagnostic). Fix S and 0<α<1/2. If for every ϵ>0, 𝔡2(T)≪ϵ,K,ST−α+ϵ holds for all sufficiently large real T, then ζK(s)≠0(Re⁡s>max⁡{1−α,1/2},s≠1). This is a strict-region implication from an explicitly hypothetical input, not a new zero-free theorem or a necessary condition for the actual signed target. With the current physical input the pure witness has the sufficient PIT majorant 19/24, and the mixed witness retains the smaller 7/9 from the minimum. Independent scalar powers U−1/12 and U−1/18 would suffice for those majorants, with compatible endpoint control; their all-scale mean-square versions would entail the strict strips 11/12 and 17/18 above. None is asserted available. The old pure 5/6 budget and U−1/6 input, with conditional strip 5/6, are historical values for the former operator bound. Proposition 40.17 gives the current global 9/8 comparison, and Proposition 40.18 the scoped A6=1 comparison 13/12. The target, principal/short assembly beyond the stated scopes, independent determinant/zero-location bridges and full analytic/category Lean formalization remain open. 40.26 Proofs for the coherent main reductions Throughout, squarefree and prime mean ideal squarefree and prime. The original symbol is extended by zero, the complete good annulus is unchanged, and the same complex W is used for every row. The common smooth divisor f is an incidence variable after ideal Möbius inversion; it is not the original column-pair gcd sector h=1. 40.26.1 Removing only the auxiliary smooth restriction The high-window support of a rough-prime term satisfies N(fa),N(fb)<2D/U≤7U. The accepted exact coefficient identity (40.76) therefore applies to these squarefree products, including the unit: AU(g)=μ(g)(2𝟏Ng≤U−1),Ng≤7U.(40.95) For completeness, every proper divisor of a nonunit good g has norm at most Ng/7≤U. The unrestricted ordered disjoint-divisor sum is ∏p∣g(1−1−1)=μ(g). If Ng>U, precisely the two assignments (g,1),(1,g) are omitted, each with weight μ(g). If Ng≤U none is omitted; g=1 is direct. This does not simplify the general annular K0 coefficients, whose norms can reach 2D. For a nonunit residual pair put M=max⁡(Na,Nb)≥7. On active rough-prime support, with F=Nf and P=Np>U, FMP<2D≤7U2, hence F<U. Such f is automatically U-smooth. Thus dropping its smoothness changes only a=b=1. There F<2D/P<7U. Norm axes are schematic, not ideal counts; a common prime gives a raw zero. The displayed tail is the normalized Gauss moment, not an energy or the raw numerator. The bound uses the explicitly cited external cubic sieve. At U≥D1/8U\ge D^{1/8} the choice Y=D1/8Y=D^{1/8} fits the stated pure critical error budget; if Y=UY=U the coefficient tail is zero.
